lead: Most electric power is produced by turning an energy source into mechanical rotation, then into alternating voltage. Solar photovoltaic is the exception: light is converted straight into DC electricity, with no moving part. Coal and nuclear are non-renewable: the fuel is used once. Solar and wind are renewable: nature refills the source. The choice affects fuel cost, emissions, land and reliability. In India, coal supplies most generation, while solar and wind are growing additions. This chapter follows the main energy converters and compares them.
prereq: You need Unit 3, Magnetic Circuits and Electrical Machines, for the synchronous generator, and Unit 2, Single-Phase and Three-Phase AC Circuits, for AC generation.

blocks.text: A coal thermal plant burns coal to make steam, and steam drives a turbine. The turbine turns a synchronous generator. The generator makes AC. This chain is a heat engine: fuel heat becomes steam, then shaft work, then electrical energy.

items: Coal is burned in the furnace. Water in the boiler becomes high-pressure steam.
Steam expands through the turbine and spins its shaft.
The shaft drives a synchronous generator, which produces AC.
Exhaust steam goes to a condenser, becomes water, and is pumped back.
The generator output is stepped up by a transformer; see 6.5.

blocks.text: A nuclear plant replaces the coal furnace with a reactor. Fission of uranium releases heat. A primary coolant carries heat to a steam generator. Steam then drives a turbine and generator. Nuclear fuel is finite, so nuclear is non-renewable. The condenser and steam loop work as in a coal plant.

blocks.where: η is overall efficiency, no unit, often written as a percentage; E<sub>out</sub> is electrical energy delivered in kWh or J; E<sub>in</sub> is fuel energy input in the same unit.

blocks.text: A photovoltaic (PV) cell is a large PN junction. Light creates electron-hole pairs; the junction separates them and gives DC voltage. Cells are connected in series for voltage and in parallel for current to form a module. Modules form an array. Irradiance is sunlight power per unit area, in W/m². Standard test irradiance is 1000 W/m². High cell temperature lowers voltage and output.

A wind turbine converts kinetic energy of moving air. Blades turn a hub. A gearbox matches low blade speed to generator speed. The generator makes AC. Cut-in speed is the lowest wind speed at which output starts. Rated speed is the wind speed at which the turbine reaches rated power. Above cut-out speed the turbine stops to protect itself.

blocks.where: P<sub>wind</sub> is wind power in W; ρ is air density in kg/m³; A is swept rotor area in m²; v is wind speed in m/s. Actual electrical power is lower by the power coefficient C<sub>p</sub>.

blocks.text: Hydro uses falling water to spin a turbine. Biomass burns plant or waste fuel to make steam. Both are renewable when managed. Rajasthan solar parks and Tamil Nadu wind farms are Indian examples.

Capital cost is the build cost. Fuel cost is the running cost. Availability is how firm the output is. Emissions and land are side effects. Coal has a large fuel bill per kWh and high emissions; fuel is cheap per kg but used in bulk. Nuclear has high build cost and radioactive waste. Solar and wind have no fuel cost but weather-dependent output.

blocks.text: Capacity in MW is power. Energy in MWh is power × time. A 100 MW plant running for 1 h gives 100 MWh. Solar and wind are rated at standard conditions, not at average site output.

examples.question: A coal thermal plant has overall efficiency 35%. The coal used has calorific value 25 MJ/kg. Find the mass of coal needed to generate 1 kWh of electrical energy.
steps: Convert electrical energy: 1 kWh = 1000 W × 3600 s = 3.6 × 10⁶ J = 3.6 MJ.
Use η = E<sub>out</sub> ÷ E<sub>in</sub>, so E<sub>in</sub> = E<sub>out</sub> ÷ η.
Coal mass = E<sub>in</sub> ÷ calorific value = 10.2857 MJ ÷ 25 MJ/kg = 0.4114 kg.
Round to three decimal places: 0.411 kg.
examples.answer: About 0.411 kg of coal is needed per kWh generated.
examples.check:
eta = 0.35
E_out_MJ = 3.6
E_in_MJ = E_out_MJ / eta
coal_kg = E_in_MJ / 25
print(round(coal_kg, 3))

traps: MW is power, MWh is energy. A 100 MW plant is not 100 MWh unless it runs for one hour.
Nuclear fission uses finite uranium, so nuclear is non-renewable even though it has low CO₂ at the plant.
Overall efficiency is output divided by input. Do not invert the fraction.
Solar and wind are rated at standard conditions or rated wind speed, not at average weather output.
Coal calorific value is energy per kg, in MJ/kg. It is not power in MW.

quiz.q: Define renewable and non-renewable energy sources.
quiz.a: A renewable source is refilled by nature within a short time, such as solar, wind, hydro or biomass. A non-renewable source is used once and is finite, such as coal, oil, gas or uranium.

quiz.q: Why does a coal thermal plant need a condenser?
quiz.a: The condenser turns exhaust steam back into water. This lowers pressure after the turbine, keeps the steam cycle closed, and lets the boiler be fed with the same water.

quiz.q: What is the difference between cut-in speed and rated speed of a wind turbine?
quiz.a: Cut-in speed is the lowest wind speed at which the turbine starts producing useful output. Rated speed is the wind speed at which it reaches its rated power.

quiz.q: A coal plant has overall efficiency 30%. Coal calorific value is 20 MJ/kg. Find coal needed per kWh generated.
quiz.a: 1 kWh = 3.6 MJ. Input = 3.6 ÷ 0.30 = 12 MJ. Coal = 12 ÷ 20 = 0.60 kg per kWh.

quiz.q: A PV module gives 100 W at standard test irradiance 1000 W/m². Ignore temperature effects. Estimate its output at 800 W/m².
quiz.a: Output scales with irradiance: 100 W × (800 ÷ 1000) = 80 W.

quiz.q: Why does a 100 MW solar park not deliver 100 MW all day?
quiz.a: Its rating is at standard irradiance. Irradiance changes with time, clouds and season, so actual output follows the sun and is below rating for most hours.

quiz.q: Compare coal and solar PV on fuel cost and availability.
quiz.a: Coal has a fuel cost and firm output that can run day and night, but high emissions. Solar has zero fuel cost and no direct emissions in use, but output is weather-dependent and not firm without storage.

beyond: Not for the exam. Grid operators balance variable solar and wind with storage, demand response and flexible coal or gas. Modern farms use hybrid solar-wind plants and weather forecasts. Research areas include perovskite cells, offshore wind, green hydrogen and levelized cost of electricity. Search for capacity factor, grid code and net metering.
